review_notes: I read all of L2.lean. I also read the definitions of fz, gz and hz in Hilbert/Defs.lean, and rescale, rescaledZeros and rescaledMult in Zeta/Defs.lean. I grepped for every use of rescaledZerosFinset in LeanPool. The private twist lemmas and the memLp lemmas have no simp-interface issues I could justify. The single finding concerns the simp interface of rescaledZerosFinset. I did not run Lean. The claim that the existing coe simp lemma does not fire on membership goals rests on Finset.mem_coe's simp direction, which I recalled rather than looked up.

findings.excerpt:
theorem coe_rescaledZerosFinset (T : ℝ) :
    ((rescaledZerosFinset T : Finset ℂ) : Set ℂ) = rescaledZeros T := by
findings.problem: The only simp lemma for `rescaledZerosFinset` is the coercion-to-`Set` equation. The goals that actually come up are membership goals `w ∈ rescaledZerosFinset T`, and the coercion lemma does not rewrite those. `Finset.mem_coe` normalises `a ∈ ↑s` towards the Finset side, so the simp set has no rule that turns `w ∈ rescaledZerosFinset T` into `w ∈ rescaledZeros T`. There is also no `mem_` lemma. As a result, every consumer unfolds the definition by hand and rebuilds the same simp set `rescaledZerosFinset, Finset.mem_image, Set.Finite.mem_toFinset`. The three fields of `isConjInvariant_rescaledZerosFinset` do this at lines 2144, 2151 and 2158. `card_simpleRealPart_rescaled_eq_simpleOnLineCount` does it at 1643, and `sum_rescaledMult_eq_zeroCount` and the card lemma use `rw [rescaledZerosFinset, ...]`. Unfolding exposes `toFinset` and `image`, which is the implementation detail this definition is meant to hide.
findings.proposed_change: Add a membership lemma next to the coercion lemma, e.g. `@[simp] theorem mem_rescaledZerosFinset {T : ℝ} {w : ℂ} : w ∈ rescaledZerosFinset T ↔ w ∈ rescaledZeros T`. Prove it via `← Finset.mem_coe, coe_rescaledZerosFinset`, or by unfolding once. Simp then normalises to the `Set` form. `rescaledZeros` is a plain def and is not unfolded by simp, so the rule cannot loop. If simp should reach the explicit witness form, a second non-simp lemma `mem_rescaledZerosFinset_iff : w ∈ rescaledZerosFinset T ↔ ∃ ρ ∈ nontrivialZeros T, rescale T ρ = w` can be used with `simp only`. Then replace the repeated `simp only [rescaledZerosFinset, Finset.mem_image, Set.Finite.mem_toFinset] at hz` calls in `AlphaExpansion.lean` with `simp only [mem_rescaledZerosFinset_iff] at hz`.
findings.benefit: Membership in the Finset gets one canonical, tested normal form. Downstream proofs no longer unfold `rescaledZerosFinset`, so they do not depend on its `toFinset.image` construction. The five-fold duplicated simp set disappears. A plain `simp` on membership goals works, which the current coercion-only interface does not allow.

evidence.excerpt: simp only [rescaledZerosFinset, Finset.mem_image, Set.Finite.mem_toFinset] at hz ⊢
noncomputable def rescaledZeros (T : ℝ) : Set ℂ := rescale T '' nontrivialZeros T
